subject: math
cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
intro: To describe a data set you report three things: its shape (symmetric, skewed left, or skewed right), its center (the mean $\bar{x}=\frac{\sum x_i}{n}$ or the median), and its spread (the range, the interquartile range $\text{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1$, or the standard deviation). An outlier is a value far from the rest; the $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ rule flags any point below $Q_1-1.5\cdot\text{IQR}$ or above $Q_3+1.5\cdot\text{IQR}$. The mean and range get pulled toward outliers, while the median and IQR resist them, so for skewed data we summarize with the median and IQR.

items.prompt: A dot plot of daily high temperatures piles up most of its dots at the warm (high) end, with a long tail trailing off toward the cold (low) values. Describe the shape of this distribution.

steps: The shape of a distribution is named for the direction of its tail, not where the bulk of the data sits.
Here most dots cluster at the high end, and the tail stretches toward the low values.
A tail pointing toward the lower numbers means the distribution is skewed to the left.
So the distribution is skewed left (also called negatively skewed).

items.prompt: For the data set $\{4,\ 6,\ 6,\ 7,\ 9,\ 12\}$, find the mean, the median, and the range.

steps: The data are already sorted and there are $n=6$ values.
Mean: add the values, $4+6+6+7+9+12=44$, then divide by $n$: $\bar{x}=\frac{44}{6}=\frac{22}{3}\approx 7.33$.
Median: with an even $n$, average the two middle values (the $3$rd and $4$th), which are $6$ and $7$: $\frac{6+7}{2}=6.5$.
Range: largest minus smallest, $12-4=8$.
So the mean is $\frac{22}{3}$, the median is $6.5$, and the range is $8$.

items.prompt: A data set of test scores has $Q_1=12$ and $Q_3=20$. Use the $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ rule to decide whether the value $35$ is an outlier.

steps: First find the interquartile range: $\text{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1=20-12=8$.
Compute $1.5\times\text{IQR}=1.5\cdot 8=12$.
Upper fence: $Q_3+1.5\cdot\text{IQR}=20+12=32$.
Lower fence: $Q_1-1.5\cdot\text{IQR}=12-12=0$.
A value is an outlier if it falls below the lower fence ($0$) or above the upper fence ($32$).
Since $35>32$, the value $35$ lies above the upper fence, so it is an outlier.
solution.answer: Yes; $35>32$ (the upper fence), so it is an outlier.

items.prompt: The data set $\{8,\ 9,\ 10,\ 11,\ 12\}$ has mean $10$ and median $10$. The value $12$ is replaced by $42$, giving $\{8,\ 9,\ 10,\ 11,\ 42\}$. Find the new mean and the new median, and explain what happened.

steps: The mean jumped from $10$ to $16$ because the extreme value $42$ pulls the mean toward it.
New median: sort the new data, $8,\ 9,\ 10,\ 11,\ 42$; the middle (3rd) value is still $10$.
The median stayed at $10$ because it depends only on the position of the middle value, not on how far the largest value moved.
This shows the mean is sensitive to outliers while the median is resistant to them.
solution.answer: New mean $=16$; new median $=10$. The mean rose toward the outlier; the median did not change.

items.prompt: Home prices in a neighborhood are strongly skewed right because a few mansions sell for far more than the typical house. Which measure of center and which measure of spread best summarize these prices, and why?

steps: When data are strongly skewed, a few extreme values distort the mean and the range.
The mean is pulled toward the high mansion prices, so it overstates a typical home price; the median is not affected by those extremes.
The range only depends on the maximum and minimum, so a single mansion inflates it; the IQR uses only the middle $50\%$ of the data and resists extremes.
Therefore the resistant measures, the median (center) and the IQR (spread), describe the typical home and its variability more fairly.
Choose the median and the IQR because they are resistant to the right skew and the extreme high prices.
solution.answer: Median for center and IQR for spread, because they are resistant to the skew and the extreme high prices.

items.prompt: A histogram of household incomes has a tall cluster of bars at the low end and a long tail stretching toward the high incomes. Describe the shape of the distribution.
items.hint: Name the shape for the side the tail points toward, not where most of the data sits.

steps: Most of the data sit at the low end, and the tail extends toward the high values.
A tail pointing toward the larger numbers means the distribution is skewed to the right.
So the distribution is skewed right (positively skewed).

items.prompt: For the data set $\{3,\ 5,\ 8,\ 8,\ 11\}$, find the mean, the median, and the range.
items.hint: Sort first (already sorted here). With an odd number of values the median is the single middle value.

steps: There are $n=5$ values and they are sorted.
Median: the middle (3rd) value of the five sorted values is $8$.
So the mean is $7$, the median is $8$, and the range is $8$.

items.prompt: A data set has $Q_1=30$ and $Q_3=46$. Use the $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ rule to decide whether the value $5$ is an outlier.
items.hint: Find the IQR, then the lower fence $Q_1-1.5\cdot\text{IQR}$. A value below the lower fence is an outlier.

steps: $1.5\times\text{IQR}=1.5\cdot 16=24$.
Lower fence: $Q_1-1.5\cdot\text{IQR}=30-24=6$.
A value is an outlier if it is below the lower fence ($6$).
Since $5<6$, the value $5$ falls below the lower fence, so it is an outlier.
solution.answer: Yes; $5<6$ (the lower fence), so it is an outlier.

items.prompt: The data set $\{20,\ 21,\ 22,\ 23,\ 24\}$ has mean $22$ and median $22$. The value $24$ is replaced by $54$, giving $\{20,\ 21,\ 22,\ 23,\ 54\}$. Find the new mean and the new median.
items.hint: Recompute the mean by adding all five values. For the median, keep the data sorted and take the middle value.

steps: The mean rose from $22$ to $28$ because the value $54$ pulls it upward.
New median: the sorted data are $20,\ 21,\ 22,\ 23,\ 54$; the middle (3rd) value is still $22$.
The median stays at $22$ because it does not depend on how large the top value is.

items.prompt: Class A scores have median $78$ and $\text{IQR}=6$. Class B scores have median $78$ and $\text{IQR}=20$. Compare the two classes. Did they perform identically?
items.hint: Equal centers do not mean equal distributions. Compare the spreads to judge consistency.

steps: Both classes have the same median, $78$, so their centers (typical scores) match.
Spread differs: Class A has $\text{IQR}=6$ while Class B has $\text{IQR}=20$.
A larger IQR means the middle $50\%$ of scores is spread over a wider range, so Class B's scores vary much more.
They did not perform identically; Class B is far more variable, so its scores are less consistent than Class A's even though the centers are equal.
solution.answer: No. The centers are equal (median $78$), but Class B has a much larger spread ($\text{IQR}=20$ vs $6$), so its scores are far less consistent.
